title: Investigate and hotfix fairness-induced throughput collapse for long-conversation workloads
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Multiple customers reported a tokens/sec collapse and elevated TTFT for multi-turn conversations with long context windows. Issue observed across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments after the scheduler change that introduced dynamic packing and cross-model kernel selection optimizations. Symptoms: sustained tokens/sec drop (~40-70%), increased first-token latency for active sessions, and slow drain of multiplex queues leading to request piling and unfair tenant starvation.
reproduction_steps: Deploy runtime with scheduler v1.24.3 and quantized kernels enabled
Start 50 concurrent chat sessions across three model families (gpt-like-8k, llama-like-16k, opt-like-32k) mixing short and long contexts
Send long-context priming requests (6k-12k tokens) on 20% of sessions and frequent short requests on remaining sessions
Observe tokens/sec on affected GPU nodes and tail TTFT on dashboard (tokens/sec metric and first_token_latency_percentile)
Expected: modest variation; Observed: sustained reduction in aggregate tokens/sec and first-token latency spike for long-context sessions
telemetry_observations: KV cache pressure correlated with long-context sessions; eviction jitter observed
Kernel selector favored smaller int8 kernels for short requests which increased fragmentation later when long streams arrived
Scheduler’s dynamic packing merged heterogeneous requests into shared microbatches leading to cross-request preemption and anti-fairness
Multiplex queue depth rose by 3x on affected hosts before throughput collapse
No memory OOMs; CUDA utilization dropped by ~22% during collapse window
steps_taken: Scoped impact: validated across hosted/dedicated/private via canary fleets and customer traces
Immediate mitigation: rolled out runtime config override to disable dynamic packing for streams with concurrent long-context priming (hotfix flag)
Backed out kernel packing heuristic in the scheduler for affected node classes (tagged gpu-xlarge)
Implemented quick affinity hack: pin long-context sessions to isolated multiplex lanes to avoid mixing with short bursts
Deployed canary hotfix to 10% of fleet and monitored metrics for 2 hours (positive improvement: tokens/sec recovered ~55% on canaries)
playbook: 01 - Ramp canary to 10% with hotfix flag and monitor tokens/sec & first_token_latency_percentile
02 - If canary stable for 2h, incrementally rollout to 50% and run regression test suite (long-conv, short-burst, mixed)
03 - Coordinate with Dedicated infra lead to push config to customer-specific fleets (some require change windows)
04 - Notify PM/Support with incident summary and temporary mitigation steps for customers (support playbook link)
05 - Post-rollout: create follow-up ticket for scheduler rewrite and test harness to avoid recurrence
acceptance_criteria: Aggregate tokens/sec on previously affected fleets returns to within 10% of baseline under the same synthetic load
First-token 95th percentile latency reduces to baseline+15% under mixed workload
No regression introduced for short-burst workloads (throughput and TTFT unchanged or improved)
Hotfix documented and rolled out with rollback plan and owner assigned
Follow-up design doc created for scheduler fairness rewrite and dedicated test harness
